clean_story:
"Proof by contradiction. Diagonalization exposes limits.

The name comes from writing numbers in a grid, then reading along the diagonal to create a new number that breaks the pattern. Imagine listing all fractions between zero and one as endless decimals. Diagonalization picks the first digit of the first number, the second digit of the second, and so on, then flips each digit to make a number that wasn’t in the original list. This proves some infinities are larger than others. Cantor used this method in 1874 to show that the infinity of real numbers outstrips the infinity of counting numbers. The technique also reveals unsolvable problems, like the halting problem in computing, where no program can predict if another will finish or run forever. Three related subjects are infinity sizes, computability theory and proof techniques."
